CREATE VIEW v_scan_ledger AS
-- v_scan_ledger: one row per (source in scope) x (active parameter).
--
--   source in scope   evidence_sources with superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL. A tombstone is
--                     never read again; its replacement is.
--   active parameter  base_parameters.status = 'active'. Retired and merged parameters
--                     leave the ledger (their extractions stay, as history).
--
-- STATUS PRECEDENCE, first match wins:
--   1 EXTRACTED          a non-absent extraction exists for the pair (any figure_role).
--   2 STATED-ABSENT      only claim_type 'absent' extractions exist: the source addresses
--                        the quantity and sets nothing -- a positive statement.
--   3 READ-NOTHING-FOUND a FULL-scope reading covers the pair and found no row.
--   4 BLOCKED            no full reading covers the pair AND the source carries an obstacle
--                        processing_blocked_reason (below): the full text could not be
--                        obtained or read, so the pair is not reading debt until a full
--                        reading is recorded. Any partial / fragment / abstract reading of
--                        the pair is still named in scan_id / text_scope / method.
--   5 READ-PARTIAL       only partial / fragment / abstract readings cover it, and no
--                        obstacle stands: the full text is obtainable and unread -- debt.
--   6 NOT-READ           no reading covers it.
-- WHY THIS ORDER (it is derived from what each fact proves; 122 ranked BLOCKED above every
-- reading and 123 below every reading, both guesses): a FULL reading proves the obstacle
-- gone, since the whole text was read, so 3 outranks 4. A partial, fragment or abstract
-- reading proves nothing about the full text, so under a standing obstacle 4 outranks 5.
-- A reading COVERS a pair when it is catalogue-mode with catalogue_version >= parameter_id
-- (the parameter existed when the reading was made), or targeted at that parameter. Rows 1
-- and 2 win over readings because a row written is stronger evidence than a reading
-- recorded; 3 wins over the rest because a full reading supersedes a partial one.
--
-- THE BLOCKED CASE BELOW IS THE ONE HOME of "the text could not be obtained or read", and
-- this header is the ONE HOME of the classification of every processing_blocked_reason
-- value (evidence_sources CHECK, migration 091); each value appears here as a bare token
-- under exactly one head, and a test derives the CHECK and fails on a value this header
-- does not name. The writers and gates read this view's status, never the column. NOTHING
-- CLEARS THE COLUMN: it is the retrieval record and stays as history; the ledger alone says
-- whether a pair is still blocked.
--   obstacle to the text (BLOCKED, above):  no-full-text, paywalled, language.
--   copy of a typed fact (not an obstacle; the writers refuse it by pointer -- the judgement
--     lives in db.py _BLOCK_REASON_COPIES): no-quantified-claims -> a recorded full reading;
--     superseded -> superseded_by_ref_id.
--   pending owner question 8 of the round-3 adjudication, treated as NULL (the source owes
--     its reading): out-of-scope, tier-not-required (they say no text was unobtainable);
--     no-doi, not-indexed (migration 091's comments describe discovery -- "no resolvable
--     identifier for automated paths", "absent from the indexes the pipeline queries" --
--     not an obstacle to a text in hand, and a URL-only report admitted without a DOI can
--     be read).
--
-- scan_id / text_scope / method name the STRONGEST covering reading (full scope first,
-- then full-read before pre-screen, then the latest), so a READ-NOTHING-FOUND resting on
-- a pre-screen only is visible as such. NULL when no reading covers the pair.
WITH pairs AS (
    SELECT e.ref_id, p.parameter_id, e.processing_blocked_reason
      FROM evidence_sources e
     CROSS JOIN base_parameters p
     WHERE e.superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL
       AND p.status = 'active'
),
best AS (
    SELECT pr.ref_id, pr.parameter_id, pr.processing_blocked_reason,
           (SELECT s.scan_id FROM source_scans s
             WHERE s.ref_id = pr.ref_id
               AND ((s.mode = 'catalogue' AND s.catalogue_version >= pr.parameter_id)
                 OR (s.mode = 'targeted' AND s.target_parameter_id = pr.parameter_id))
             ORDER BY (s.text_scope = 'full') DESC, (s.method = 'full-read') DESC,
                      s.scan_id DESC
             LIMIT 1) AS scan_id
      FROM pairs pr
)
SELECT b.ref_id,
       b.parameter_id,
       CASE
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type <> 'absent') THEN 'EXTRACTED'
         WHEN EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM source_value_extractions x
                       WHERE x.ref_id = b.ref_id AND x.parameter_id = b.parameter_id
                         AND x.claim_type = 'absent') THEN 'STATED-ABSENT'
         WHEN s.text_scope = 'full' THEN 'READ-NOTHING-FOUND'
         WHEN b.processing_blocked_reason IN
              ('no-full-text', 'paywalled', 'language') THEN 'BLOCKED'
         WHEN s.scan_id IS NOT NULL THEN 'READ-PARTIAL'
         ELSE 'NOT-READ'
       END AS status,
       b.scan_id,
       s.text_scope,
       s.method
  FROM best b
  LEFT JOIN source_scans s ON s.scan_id = b.scan_id
CREATE TABLE source_scans (
    -- AUTOINCREMENT, as 076 did for the other ids a record names: a scan_id is cited by
    -- session records and must never come to mean a different reading.
    scan_id             INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    ref_id              TEXT    NOT NULL REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id),
    -- catalogue: every active parameter up to catalogue_version.
    -- targeted:  one parameter, target_parameter_id (a back-fill reading).
    mode                TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (mode IN ('catalogue', 'targeted')),
    catalogue_version   INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (catalogue_version >= 1),
    target_parameter_id INTEGER REFERENCES base_parameters(parameter_id),
    -- full: the whole document. partial: some pages of it. fragment: one page or clause
    -- of a larger instrument. abstract: an abstract or metadata record only.
    text_scope          TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (text_scope IN
                                ('full', 'partial', 'fragment', 'abstract')),
    pages_read          INTEGER CHECK (pages_read IS NULL OR pages_read >= 0),
    pages_total         INTEGER CHECK (pages_total IS NULL OR pages_total >= 1),
    -- Which saved file was read, by checksum: the manifest's own sha256 of the bytes.
    file_sha256         TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (length(file_sha256) = 64),
    -- Whether the open pass (quantities the catalogue lacks, plan section 3.4) was done
    -- in this reading.
    open_pass_done      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (open_pass_done IN (0, 1)),
    -- full-read: the text was read against the list. pre-screen: only a script listed
    -- where catalogue terms occur -- weaker, and v_scan_ledger says which it was.
    method              TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (method IN ('full-read', 'pre-screen')),
    notes               TEXT,
    created_at          TEXT    NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT    NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT,
    updated_by_session  TEXT,
    CHECK ((mode = 'targeted' AND target_parameter_id IS NOT NULL)
        OR (mode = 'catalogue' AND target_parameter_id IS NULL)),
    CHECK (pages_read IS NULL OR pages_total IS NULL OR pages_read <= pages_total),
    -- "full" over a paged text means every page; a reading of fewer pages is partial.
    CHECK (text_scope <> 'full' OR pages_read IS NULL OR pages_read = pages_total)
)
CREATE TABLE term_adjudications (
    adjudication_id     INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    observation_id      INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES observed_terms(observation_id),
    -- OUTCOMES, documented HERE and not inside the CHECK. dbcore.check_values() reads
    -- this constraint's own value list to build the CLI's refusal, and an inline
    -- comment between the quoted values defeats its parser -- measured 2026-09-03,
    -- when a first cut of this migration carried the descriptions inside the IN(...)
    -- and every legitimate outcome was refused with a mangled vocabulary. The whole
    -- reason vocabularies come from the schema rather than a list in the code
    -- (CLAUDE.md §4) is defeated by punctuation the parser cannot see past.
    --
    --   NAMES-EXISTING  names a term we already hold
    --   NAMES-NEW       names a concept new to the vocabulary
    --   NOT-OURS        a real phrase, but not one of our concepts
    --   DEFERRED        cannot be settled on this source alone
    outcome             TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (outcome IN
                            ('NAMES-EXISTING','NAMES-NEW','NOT-OURS','DEFERRED')),
    term_id             TEXT REFERENCES terms(term_id),
    -- NOT NULL: an adjudication that does not say why cannot be contested, and the
    -- whole point of splitting observation from judgment is that the judgement is
    -- inspectable.
    rationale           TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT,
    updated_by_session  TEXT,
    -- The outcome and the pointer must agree. An outcome that names a term must name
    -- one; an outcome that declines must not.
    CHECK (
        (outcome IN ('NAMES-EXISTING','NAMES-NEW') AND term_id IS NOT NULL)
     OR (outcome IN ('NOT-OURS','DEFERRED')        AND term_id IS NULL)
    )
)
CREATE TABLE "observed_terms" (
    observation_id      INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
    -- POINTER, not a copy. The source's bibliography stays in evidence_sources.
    ref_id              TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id),
    -- The phrase EXACTLY as the source writes it. Not normalised, not translated,
    -- not mapped. R11 forbids back-translation and this is where that starts.
    surface_form        TEXT NOT NULL,
    -- The language the phrase APPEARS IN, which need not be the source's language.
    language            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'EN',
    -- R3's locator discipline: where in the source it appears. Part of the sighting's
    -- key since migration 102 (ux_observed_terms_sighting below).
    locator             TEXT,
    -- Enough surrounding text that judgment can adjudicate without re-retrieving.
    context_quote       TEXT,
    notes               TEXT,
    created_at          TEXT NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT NOT NULL,
    updated_at          TEXT,
    updated_by_session  TEXT
)
CREATE TABLE "search_executions" (
  exec_id              INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  slug                 TEXT REFERENCES slugs(slug),   -- NULL when the search is for a parameter or mines a source (R43)
  parameter_id         INTEGER REFERENCES base_parameters(parameter_id),   -- the parameter a slug-less search was FOR (R43)
  jurisdiction         TEXT,                 -- NULL = jurisdiction-agnostic search
  language             TEXT NOT NULL,        -- ISO; one of the 19 research languages
  -- hierarchy branch the search TARGETED (diffable against what was FOUND):
  target_tier          INTEGER CHECK (target_tier IS NULL OR target_tier BETWEEN 1 AND 6),
  target_evidence_type TEXT CHECK (target_evidence_type IS NULL OR target_evidence_type IN
     ('clinical','sr_meta','standard_eb','national_fw','code','co1','co2','grey')),
  target_scope         TEXT CHECK (target_scope IS NULL OR target_scope IN
     ('intrinsic','lower_control','high_control','national','international')),
  -- the verbatim, replayable query:
  query_text           TEXT NOT NULL,
  terms_used           TEXT,                 -- JSON array of term ids
  engine               TEXT NOT NULL,        -- pubmed|crossref|scholar|biorxiv|medrxiv|consensus|web|registry|manual
  -- depth as real method, not booleans:
  depth_method         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (depth_method IN ('scoping','systematic')),
  mining_direction     TEXT CHECK (mining_direction IS NULL OR mining_direction IN
     ('none','backward','forward','both')),
  -- yield:
  results_found        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  results_screened     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  results_admitted     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  saturation_signal    TEXT CHECK (saturation_signal IS NULL OR saturation_signal IN
     ('none','partial','saturated')),
  admitted_ref_ids     TEXT,                 -- JSON array of evidence_sources.ref_id
  deferred_reason      TEXT,                 -- non-NULL => deliberate no-search for this cell
  backfill             INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (backfill IN (0,1)),
  created_by_session              TEXT NOT NULL,
  created_at          TEXT NOT NULL, findings_note TEXT, harm_finding INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0, prior_expectation TEXT, origin TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'planned'
  CHECK (origin IN ('planned','incidental','adversarial-pass','owner-supplied','lead-index')), mined_ref_id TEXT REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id), origin_pass_id INTEGER
  REFERENCES adversarial_passes(pass_id) CHECK (origin_pass_id IS NULL OR origin = 'adversarial-pass'), updated_at TEXT, updated_by_session TEXT, identity_code TEXT REFERENCES "base_taxonomy_identity"(identity_code), icf_code TEXT REFERENCES base_icf(icf_code), needs_code TEXT REFERENCES access_needs(need_code), absence_class TEXT
  CHECK (absence_class IS NULL OR absence_class IN ('query_shape_failure', 'wrong_index', 'genuine_absence'))
  CHECK (absence_class IS NULL OR results_found = 0), gap_id TEXT REFERENCES gaps(gap_id),        -- explicit ISO ts (deterministic under rebuild)
  CHECK (terms_used IS NULL OR json_valid(terms_used)),
  CHECK (admitted_ref_ids IS NULL OR json_valid(admitted_ref_ids)),
  CHECK (COALESCE(slug, parameter_id, mined_ref_id) IS NOT NULL)   -- a search says what it is for (R43)
) STRICT
CREATE TABLE "citation_mining" (
    slug                TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES slugs(slug),
    local_ref_id        TEXT NOT NULL,

def record_scan(data: dict, session: str, dry_run: bool = False):
    """Record one READING of one source against the parameter list (migration 103).

    The scan contract (catalogue-plan-v2 section 3; owner 2026-10-09: "Slugs guide our
    searches, but they do not guide what we derive and mine from sources!"): every
    admitted source is read against the whole catalogue, and each reading leaves this
    record, from which v_scan_ledger derives, for every (source, active parameter), in this
    precedence (migration 124): EXTRACTED, STATED-ABSENT, READ-NOTHING-FOUND, BLOCKED,
    READ-PARTIAL, NOT-READ.

    THIS VERB WRITES source_scans AND NOTHING ELSE. Nothing clears
    `evidence_sources.processing_blocked_reason`: it is the retrieval record (why the full
    text could not be had), written at admission or by `amend-source`, and a reading is a
    different fact about a different thing. The ledger decides which still holds: a FULL
    reading proves the obstacle gone and outranks the block; a partial, fragment or abstract
    reading does not, so the pair reads BLOCKED with this reading's scan beside it ("abstract
    read, full text paywalled"). A judgment-stage verb never updates an evidence-stage row.

    COMPUTED, NEVER TYPED (CLAUDE.md rule 8): `catalogue_version` is the highest
    parameter_id at call time (ids are never reissued, so it says exactly which parameters
    the reading could have covered), and pages read / pages total come from the file's
    own page markers (retrieval_log.page_coverage) and, for a text derived from a PDF,
    the PDF's page count.

    REFUSES: a typed catalogue version; an unknown or superseded source (a tombstone is
    never read again); a mode, scope or method outside the column's CHECK; a targeted
    reading with no target, or a target that is not active; a catalogue reading when no
    parameter exists; a --file-sha256 that is not a file the retrieval-log manifests hold
    for this source, or whose bytes on disk no longer hash to it; `full` over a fetched file
    (what was read of a PDF or a landing page is not knowable from the bytes: derive its text
    with scripts/research/full_text.py and read that) and `full` over a text with fewer pages
    than the document it was derived from. A `full` over a text with no page markers lands as
    the operator's claim and the result says `uncounted`: nothing here counted it.
    """
    if data.get("catalogue_version") is not None:
        raise Refusal(
            "record-scan: the catalogue version is COMPUTED, never typed -- it is the "
            "highest parameter_id when the reading is recorded (CLAUDE.md rule 8). A typed "
            "one could claim a reading covered parameters it never saw. Drop "
            "--catalogue-version. Nothing was written.")
    sha = (data.get("file_sha256") or "").strip().lower()
    if not re.fullmatch(r"[0-9a-f]{64}", sha):
        raise Refusal("record-scan: --file-sha256 must be the full sha256 (64 hex "
                      "characters) of the saved file read, as the manifest records it.")
    mode = data.get("mode")
    target = data.get("target_parameter_id")
    retrieval_log = _retrieval_log()
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        ref = dbcore.fold_ref(data.get("ref_id"))
        src = conn.execute("SELECT ref_id, url FROM evidence_sources WHERE ref_id = ?",
                           (ref,)).fetchone()
        if src is None:
            raise Refusal(f"record-scan: {data.get('ref_id')!r} is not an admitted source.")
        _refuse_tombstone(conn, ref, "record-scan")
        for col, flag in (("mode", "--mode"), ("text_scope", "--text-scope"),
                          ("method", "--method")):
            dbcore.check_declared(conn, "source_scans", col, data.get(col),
                                  f"record-scan {flag}")
        top = conn.execute("SELECT MAX(parameter_id) FROM base_parameters").fetchone()[0]
        if top is None:
            raise Refusal("record-scan: base_parameters holds no rows, so there is no "
                          "catalogue to read a source against.")
        if mode == "targeted":
            if target is None:
                raise Refusal("record-scan: --mode targeted needs --target-parameter-id, "
                              "the one parameter this reading looked for.")
            prow = conn.execute("SELECT status FROM base_parameters WHERE parameter_id = ?",
                                (target,)).fetchone()
            if prow is None or prow["status"] != "active":
                raise Refusal(f"record-scan: --target-parameter-id {target} is "
                              f"{'not a parameter' if prow is None else prow['status']}; a "
                              f"reading is for an active parameter.")
        elif target is not None:
            raise Refusal("record-scan: --target-parameter-id is for --mode targeted; a "
                          "catalogue reading covers every active parameter up to the "
                          "catalogue version.")
        held = retrieval_log.artefacts_for_source(ref, src["url"])
        match = [h for h in held if (h["sha256"] or "").lower() == sha]
        if not match:
            listed = "; ".join(f"{h['artefact']} {h['sha256'] or '?'} ({h['via']})"
                               for h in held) or "nothing"
            raise Refusal(
                f"record-scan: no file saved for {ref} has sha256 {sha[:16]}... The reading "
                f"must name bytes the retrieval-log holds FOR this source. Saved for it: "
                f"{listed}. Give the --file-sha256 of one of them. Nothing was written.")
        h = next((m for m in match if m["exists"]), match[0])
        if not h["exists"]:
            raise Refusal(f"record-scan: {h['session']}/{h['artefact']} is in the manifest "
                          f"but not on disk. Nothing was written.")
        import hashlib                                            # noqa: E402
        if hashlib.sha256(h["path"].read_bytes()).hexdigest() != sha:
            raise Refusal(f"record-scan: {h['session']}/{h['artefact']} no longer hashes "
                          f"to its manifest sha256. Nothing was written.")
        pages_read, pages_total = retrieval_log.page_coverage(h["path"])
        if h["derived"] and h["derived_from"] and pages_read is not None:
            sd, srec = retrieval_log.find_fetched_artefact(
                h["derived_from"], prefer_dir=retrieval_log.LOG_ROOT / h["session"])
            if srec is not None and srec["artefact"].lower().endswith(".pdf"):
                held_pages = retrieval_log.pdf_page_count(sd / srec["artefact"])
                if held_pages:
                    pages_total = max(pages_total or 0, held_pages)
        scope = data.get("text_scope")
        if scope == "full":
            if not h["derived"]:
                # NOT ONLY A PDF. A fetched HTML page is a publisher's landing page as
                # often as it is the document (a repository record was recorded `full`
                # on 2026-11-06); what the whole document holds is knowable only from
                # the text full_text.py derives from it, whatever the fetched bytes were.
                raise Refusal(
                    f"record-scan: --text-scope full over a fetched file ({h['artefact']}"
                    f"{', %s pages' % pages_total if pages_total else ''}): what the whole "
                    f"document holds is not knowable from fetched bytes. Derive its text "
                    f"first -- python3 scripts/research/full_text.py --ref-id {ref} "
                    f"--session {session} -- and record the reading of that. Nothing was "
                    f"written.")
            if pages_read is not None and pages_total and pages_read < pages_total:
                raise Refusal(
                    f"record-scan: --text-scope full, but {h['artefact']} carries "
                    f"{pages_read} of {pages_total} pages. Record it as partial, or derive "
                    f"every page (scripts/research/full_text.py) and read that. Nothing "
                    f"was written.")
        row = {"ref_id": ref, "mode": mode, "catalogue_version": top,
               "target_parameter_id": target, "text_scope": scope,
               "pages_read": pages_read, "pages_total": pages_total,
               "file_sha256": sha, "open_pass_done": 1 if data.get("open_pass_done") else 0,
               "method": data.get("method"),
               "notes": (data.get("notes") or "").strip() or None}
        row.update(dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "source_scans", session))
        cur = conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO source_scans ({','.join(row)}) "
                           f"VALUES ({','.join('?' * len(row))})", list(row.values()))
        out = {"scan_id": cur.lastrowid, "ref_id": ref, "catalogue_version": top,
               "file": f"{h['session']}/{h['artefact']}", "pages_read": pages_read,
               "pages_total": pages_total, "text_scope": scope, "dry_run": dry_run}
        if scope == "full" and pages_read is None:
            out["uncounted"] = True
        return out


def _owner_approval(approval_ref: str, subject: str) -> str:
    """The approval heading for a base-vocabulary admission: one dated ledger entry whose heading begins "Owner"
    (the owner's own words). A delegated resolution is a model's, and any other entry (a session, a referral, a
    correction, a supersession record) is not an approval, so each admits nothing."""
    heading = dbcore.require_approval_heading(approval_ref, subject)
    if heading.startswith(dbcore.LEDGER_DELEGATED_PREFIX):
        raise Refusal(f"{subject}: --approval-ref {heading!r} is a delegated resolution (a model's, under the "
                      f"owner's delegation), not the owner's words. This is a decision on research scope or "
                      f"the population taxonomy, and the owner's. Nothing was written.")
    if not heading.startswith(dbcore.LEDGER_OWNER_PREFIX):
        raise Refusal(f"{subject}: --approval-ref {heading!r} is not an entry that records the owner's own words "
                      f"(the ledger's owner entries begin {dbcore.LEDGER_OWNER_PREFIX!r}: Owner answers, Owner "
                      f"statements, Owner rulings). A session heading, a referral to the owner, a correction or "
                      f"a supersession record approves nothing. List them with grep -n '^## Owner' "
                      f"references/project-standards.md. Nothing was written.")
    return heading


def add_lang_jur_pair(language: str, jurisdiction: str, role: str, notes: str, approval_ref: str,
                      session: str, dry_run: bool = False):
    """Admit one language-and-jurisdiction pair to `lang_jur_map`, pointing at the ledger entry that records
    the owner's approval. `scope_status` stays NULL (owed): scoping a pair in or out is `set-pair-scope`."""
    language, jurisdiction = (language or "").strip(), (jurisdiction or "").strip()
    if not language or language != language.upper():
        raise Refusal(f"add-lang-jur-pair: --language {language!r} must be non-blank and upper case (the letter "
                      f"case lang_jur_map holds). Nothing was written.")
    heading = _owner_approval(approval_ref, "add-lang-jur-pair")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        dbcore.check_jurisdiction(jurisdiction, "add-lang-jur-pair --jurisdiction")
        dbcore.check_declared(conn, "lang_jur_map", "role", role, "add-lang-jur-pair --role")
        _kind = conn.execute("SELECT kind, parent_code FROM base_jurisdictions WHERE jurisdiction_code=?",
                             (jurisdiction,)).fetchone()
        if _kind and _kind["kind"] == "sub-national":
            raise Refusal(f"add-lang-jur-pair: {jurisdiction!r} is a sub-national code. A pair is keyed on the "
                          f"country: coverage counts a search under a sub-national code toward its parent, so a "
                          f"pair on {jurisdiction!r} could never be satisfied. Use --jurisdiction "
                          f"{_kind['parent_code']!r}. Nothing was written.")
        if conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM lang_jur_map WHERE language=? AND jurisdiction=?",
                        (language, jurisdiction)).fetchone():
            raise Refusal(f"add-lang-jur-pair: the pair {language}/{jurisdiction} is already held. A held pair's "
                          f"role is not rewritten here. Nothing was written.")
        new_language = not conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM lang_jur_map WHERE language=?", (language,)).fetchone()
        row = {"language": language, "jurisdiction": jurisdiction, "role": role, "notes": notes or None}
        row.update(dbcore.stamp_for(conn, "lang_jur_map", session))
        conn.execute(f"INSERT INTO lang_jur_map ({','.join(row)}) VALUES ({','.join('?' * len(row))})",
                     list(row.values()))
    return {"language": language, "jurisdiction": jurisdiction, "role": role, "new_language": new_language,
            "approval_ref": heading, "dry_run": dry_run}


def set_pair_scope(language: str, jurisdiction: str, scope_status: str, approval_ref: str, session: str,
                   dry_run: bool = False):
    """Set `scope_status` of one held pair, pointing at the ledger entry that records the owner's answer."""
    heading = _owner_approval(approval_ref, "set-pair-scope")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        row = conn.execute("SELECT scope_status FROM lang_jur_map WHERE language=? AND jurisdiction=?",
                           (language, jurisdiction)).fetchone()
        if row is None:
            raise Refusal(f"set-pair-scope: the pair {language}/{jurisdiction} is not held. List the pairs with "
                          f"SELECT language, jurisdiction FROM lang_jur_map; `db.py add-lang-jur-pair` admits "
                          f"one. Nothing was written.")
        dbcore.check_declared(conn, "lang_jur_map", "scope_status", scope_status, "set-pair-scope --scope-status")
        if row["scope_status"] == scope_status:
            raise Refusal(f"set-pair-scope: {language}/{jurisdiction} is already {scope_status!r}. Nothing was "
                          f"written.")
        conn.execute("UPDATE lang_jur_map SET scope_status=? WHERE language=? AND jurisdiction=?",
                     (scope_status, language, jurisdiction))
    return {"language": language, "jurisdiction": jurisdiction, "scope_status": scope_status,
            "scope_status_was": row["scope_status"], "approval_ref": heading, "dry_run": dry_run}

def _alias_language(conn, language: str) -> str:
    """`language` in the letter case `term_aliases` itself uses, measured, not assumed.

    observed_terms stores 'EN' and term_aliases stores 'en' (catalogue-plan-v2 section
    1.2 item 4). A phrase observed in 'DE' and an alias in 'de' are the same language,
    and a primary key that compared them as different would admit the same alias twice.
    """
    lo, up = conn.execute(
        "SELECT SUM(language = lower(language)), SUM(language = upper(language)) "
        "FROM term_aliases").fetchone()
    return language.lower() if (lo or 0) >= (up or 0) else language.upper()


def _names_term(conn, observation_id: int, term_id: str) -> bool:
    """Does the LATEST adjudication of this observation name this term?

    Adjudications are appended, never edited (adjudicate_term: a disagreeing judgment is a second
    row), so the latest one is the observation's standing judgment; an earlier one that named the
    term and was later declined or re-pointed warrants nothing. Latest = highest adjudication_id
    (the order the writer assigns; created_at is minute-resolution and can tie)."""
    row = conn.execute(
        "SELECT term_id FROM term_adjudications WHERE observation_id = ? "
        "ORDER BY adjudication_id DESC LIMIT 1", (observation_id,)).fetchone()
    return row is not None and row[0] == term_id

"""A fixture retrieval-log root that a pre-admission fetch cannot reach (T-073).

A batch persists what it fetched under the id its source will take BEFORE `db.py add-source` admits the source, so between
the two the retrieval log holds an id the database does not. A fixture that mints a source through the writer takes the
database's next id, which is that folder's id, and inherits the saved text: a refusal case then goes red for a reason that
has nothing to do with what it tests. The fix is to isolate the ROOT, not to change the id: a real admission must still take
the id its folder was filed under.

`fixture_log_root(dest, db_path)` symlinks into `dest` each folder of the repository's retrieval log EXCEPT a folder whose
manifest names a ref_id above the high-water mark of the database at `db_path`; such a folder is linked file by file with
only the lines and artefacts of those ids left out, and one line is printed for each.
"""
import json
import pathlib
import re
import sqlite3
import sys

REPO = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]
sys.path.insert(0, str(REPO / "scripts"))
import dbcore  # noqa: E402


def fixture_log_root(dest, db_path, source=None):
    dest, source = pathlib.Path(dest), pathlib.Path(source or REPO / "retrieval-log")
    dest.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    ro = sqlite3.connect(f"file:{db_path}?mode=ro", uri=True)
    try:
        high = dbcore.ref_id_high_water(ro)
    finally:
        ro.close()
    for d in sorted(source.iterdir()):
        if not d.is_dir():
            continue
        manifest = d / "manifest.jsonl"
        keep, ahead, stems = [], set(), set()
        if manifest.exists():
            for line in manifest.open(encoding="utf-8"):
                if not line.strip():
                    continue
                rec = json.loads(line)
                ref = (rec.get("ref_id") or "").strip()
                m = dbcore._MINTABLE.fullmatch(ref)
                if m and int(m.group(1)) > high:
                    ahead.add(ref)
                    if rec.get("artefact"):
                        stems.add(pathlib.Path(rec["artefact"]).stem)
                else:
                    keep.append(line)
        if not ahead:
            link = dest / d.name
            if not link.exists():
                link.symlink_to(d.resolve())
            continue
        # A batch files several sources into one folder and admits them one at a time: leave out only the lines (and the
        # files) of the ids above the mark, not the artefacts of the sources already admitted (T-073 critic, 2026-11-15).
        print(f"fixture root: left out {sorted(ahead)} from {d.name} (above the copy's high-water mark {high})")
        out = dest / d.name
        out.mkdir(exist_ok=True)
        (out / "manifest.jsonl").write_text("".join(keep), encoding="utf-8")

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
scripts/generate/context_map.py — emit governance/context-map.yaml.

WHAT THIS IS. A machine-readable orientation index: where everything is, what it
is, who writes it, who reads it, and whether it is canonical or derived. It exists
so a fresh session can answer "what is this and can I trust it?" from one query
instead of by grepping a tree that hides six directories from ripgrep.

WHY IT IS GENERATED AND NOT WRITTEN. This repository's signature defect is a
document that is readable and wrong: a comment asserting a protection that was
retired, a register whose stated reasons did not survive their first audit, a
count in prose that the database contradicts. A hand-maintained context map would
join that set within a month. So every volatile field here is DERIVED at generation
time -- row counts from the live DB, check levels from the registry, writers from
the source. Nothing volatile is typed by hand.

  CLAUDE.md is the human map and says of itself "a derived map, not a source of
  truth". This is the machine map, and the same disclaimer applies with more force:
  regenerate it, do not edit it.

DETERMINISM IS THE CONTRACT. Output is a pure function of (git HEAD, the DB, the
filesystem). No wall-clock time is recorded -- the provenance line carries the
commit sha and a DB fingerprint instead. Re-running against an unchanged repo
yields a byte-identical file, which is what makes --check meaningful.

USAGE
  python3 scripts/generate/context_map.py              # write governance/context-map.yaml
  python3 scripts/generate/context_map.py --check      # exit 1 if the committed file is stale
  python3 scripts/generate/context_map.py --stdout     # print, write nothing

Exit codes: 0 ok; 1 --check found staleness; 2 config error.
"""

# The two relations that require a ROW referent, never a label -- the table's own
# CHECK (`relation NOT IN ('condition_on','derived_from') OR to_extraction_id IS NOT
# NULL`), mirrored here so the CLI can name the reason instead of letting SQLite say
# "CHECK constraint failed".
_ROW_ONLY_RELATIONS = ("condition_on", "derived_from")


def _covering_scan(conn, ref_id: str, parameter_id: int):
    """The strongest source_scans row that COVERS (ref_id, parameter_id), or None.

    One rule, the one v_scan_ledger (migration 103) states: a catalogue reading covers every
    parameter up to its catalogue_version; a targeted reading covers its target. Read here
    so add-extraction and amend-extraction refuse what the ledger would show as unread.
    """
    return conn.execute(
        "SELECT scan_id, text_scope, method FROM source_scans WHERE ref_id=? AND "
        "((mode='catalogue' AND catalogue_version>=?) OR (mode='targeted' AND "
        "target_parameter_id=?)) ORDER BY (text_scope='full') DESC, (method='full-read') "
        "DESC, scan_id DESC LIMIT 1", (ref_id, parameter_id, parameter_id)).fetchone()


def _require_full_scan_for_verified(conn, ref_id: str, parameter_id: int, context: str):
    """OR-11a (owner 2026-10-29): `verified` requires a recorded FULL-scope reading that covers
    the row's parameter. Before this, `verified` was a self-declared word nothing read."""
    scan = _covering_scan(conn, ref_id, parameter_id)
    if scan is None or scan["text_scope"] != "full":
        have = "no reading covers it" if scan is None else (
            f"the strongest covering reading is scan {scan['scan_id']} at "
            f"text_scope={scan['text_scope']!r}")
        raise Refusal(
            f"{context}: extraction_status='verified' requires a full-scope reading of "
            f"{ref_id} that covers parameter {parameter_id} (OR-11a, owner 2026-10-29); "
            f"{have}. Derive the whole text (scripts/research/full_text.py), record it "
            f"(db.py record-scan --text-scope full), then mark the row verified. Nothing "
            f"was written.")

-- 140_coverage_parameter_via_admission_repair.sql
-- SCHEMA migration, view only (a compensating migration: 139 is committed and is not edited). Repairs what the
-- read-only critic of T-067 found in v_coverage_parameter_via_admission:
--  * A SUPERSEDED SOURCE IS NOT A SECOND SOURCE (LED-171, migration 106): `reached` now joins evidence_sources and
--    keeps only sources with no superseded_by_ref_id. Live, (3, KO, KR) counted REF-01019 and its successor REF-01031,
--    one Korean annex, as two sources.
--  * A SEARCH REACHES A PARAMETER THROUGH A FIGURE A SOURCE STATES, not through a record that the source does NOT hold
--    it (claim_type 'absent') and not through a skimmed row (extraction_method 'skim'; dbcore.NOT_PUBLISHABLE_METHODS,
--    owner 2026-10-09, which a test pins against this literal). Two of parameter 8's three non-zero live pairs were
--    reached only by absence rows.
--  * A ROW OF ZEROS IS NOT "UNSEARCHED": a search that ran under a slug and admitted nothing credits no parameter.
--    searches_ran_in_pair counts every search that ran in the pair, whatever it was for, so "searched, nothing found"
--    and "not looked for" are told apart (research-log-manager: the thing the pipeline exists to preserve).
--  * jurisdiction_registered says whether the pair's jurisdiction is a declared code (a search cannot be logged in
--    one that is not), so a structural zero is not read as an unsearched pair.
-- Unchanged on purpose: a source admitted for one parameter reaches every parameter it holds a figure for (that is
-- what "through admissions" means); an UNVERIFIED source still reaches (a lead is a reach; whether it should is the
-- owner's reading of OR-8, recorded in the pull request); T-050 adds the retired_at filter to `reached`.
DROP VIEW v_coverage_parameter_via_admission;
CREATE VIEW v_coverage_parameter_via_admission AS
WITH searched AS (
  SELECT se.exec_id, se.parameter_id, UPPER(se.language) AS language,
         COALESCE(b.parent_code, se.jurisdiction) AS jurisdiction
    FROM search_executions se
    LEFT JOIN base_jurisdictions b ON b.jurisdiction_code = se.jurisdiction
   WHERE se.deferred_reason IS NULL),
reached AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT s.exec_id, s.language, s.jurisdiction, x.parameter_id, sa.ref_id
    FROM searched s
    JOIN search_admissions sa ON sa.exec_id = s.exec_id
    JOIN evidence_sources e ON e.ref_id = sa.ref_id AND e.superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL
    JOIN source_value_extractions x ON x.ref_id = sa.ref_id
   WHERE x.claim_type <> 'absent' AND COALESCE(x.extraction_method, '') <> 'skim')
SELECT p.parameter_id, v.language, v.jurisdiction, v.role,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM searched s WHERE s.language = v.language AND s.jurisdiction = v.jurisdiction)
           AS searches_ran_in_pair,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM searched s WHERE s.parameter_id = p.parameter_id
           AND s.language = v.language AND s.jurisdiction = v.jurisdiction) AS searches_naming_parameter,
       (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.exec_id) FROM reached r WHERE r.parameter_id = p.parameter_id
           AND r.language = v.language AND r.jurisdiction = v.jurisdiction) AS searches_reaching_parameter,
           AS searches_ran_in_pair,
       (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM searched s WHERE s.parameter_id = p.parameter_id
           AND s.language = v.language AND s.jurisdiction = v.jurisdiction) AS searches_naming_parameter,
       (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.exec_id) FROM reached r WHERE r.parameter_id = p.parameter_id
           AND r.language = v.language AND r.jurisdiction = v.jurisdiction) AS searches_reaching_parameter,
       (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT r.ref_id) FROM reached r WHERE r.parameter_id = p.parameter_id
           AND r.language = v.language AND r.jurisdiction = v.jurisdiction) AS sources_admitted,
       EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM base_jurisdictions j WHERE j.jurisdiction_code = v.jurisdiction) AS jurisdiction_registered
  FROM base_parameters p CROSS JOIN v_research_scope v
 WHERE p.status = 'active';

PRAGMA user_version = 140;

-- 141_reading_deferrals.sql
-- SCHEMA migration (T-079, AT-17; no data). A reading can be deferred on the record, and every deferred act lists with
-- its age from one view.
--
-- WHY. The owner (2026-09-18): a deferral is legitimate "so long as it runs eventually"; nothing in the repository
-- enforced or even measured it. A search not run and a source not mined each carried a deferral and a date; a source
-- not read had no deferred state, so "chosen not to read yet" could not be told from "nobody has looked", and no query
-- listed all of them with their age. What reaches the guidebook without it: a source whose full text is owed for a
-- parameter, deferred once, never read, and indistinguishable from one deferred last week.
--
-- reading_deferrals is a table of its own. Rejected: a source_scans row (its file_sha256 and text_scope describe a
-- reading that HAPPENED; a deferral is the opposite fact); evidence_sources.data_capture_status (one value per source,
-- no date, no reason, and a column a data migration INSERTs); a new v_scan_ledger status (the pair stays owed until it
-- is read, and every gate that reads the ledger's statuses would change meaning). A deferral is DISCHARGED BY
-- DERIVATION, never by a write: the view below drops it when a full reading covers it.
--
-- v_deferred_acts is a cross-stage pointer view (CLAUDE.md section 3): it reads research (search_executions,
-- citation_mining), evidence (evidence_sources, source_scans, reading_deferrals) and judgment (term_adjudications,
-- observed_terms), plus base (base_parameters). Nothing reads it as a gate: what age makes a standing deferral a defect
-- is the owner's to say, and no threshold is stored or typed anywhere. The age query is
--   SELECT * FROM v_deferred_acts WHERE deferred_at < datetime('now', '-<N> days') ORDER BY deferred_at;

CREATE TABLE reading_deferrals (
    deferral_id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY AUTOINCREMENT,
    ref_id              TEXT    NOT NULL REFERENCES evidence_sources(ref_id),
    -- NULL: the whole-source catalogue reading is what is deferred.
    parameter_id        INTEGER REFERENCES base_parameters(parameter_id),
    reason              TEXT    NOT NULL CHECK (trim(reason) <> ''),
    created_at          TEXT    NOT NULL,
    created_by_session  TEXT    NOT NULL
);

CREATE VIEW v_deferred_acts AS
-- v_deferred_acts: every deferral that still STANDS, one row each, with the date it was first recorded.
--   kind                subject
--   search              the exec id, with its slug when it has one
--   mining              the mined ref_id and the slug
--   reading             the ref_id and the parameter (or the whole source)
--   adjudication        the observation id, its ref_id and its surface form
-- ref_id and parameter_id are the same facts as columns, so a writer asks "is this pair already deferred?" of this
-- view and cannot disagree with it (db.py defer-reading does). They are NULL where the kind has none.
-- deferred_at is the date the obligation was FIRST recorded (created_at), never the date a row was last written: a
-- re-deferral that reset the clock would hide an old obligation. A search carries a date; the others a minute.
--
-- WHAT EACH ARM DROPS, and why (a standing deferral is one nothing has since discharged):
--   search        NOTHING. A search later run is a new row that names nothing it discharges, so every deferred
--                 search lists, including one whose cell a later search has since covered. Not derivable today.
--   mining        a row whose source's citation_mining_status is no longer 'deferred' (the owner's execution signal,
--                 2026-09-18: db.py log-mining --discharge-deferral clears the row and the status together). A row whose
--                 ref resolves to no evidence_sources row (a lead anchor) has no status to read and lists while its own
--                 deferred_reason stands. created_at is the ROW's: a row first written by a pass that ran and deferred
--                 later is dated from the pass.
--   reading       a deferral whose source is now superseded (the replacement is what is owed) or whose parameter is no
--                 longer active (the ledger drops it), and one a FULL reading dated at or after the deferral covers:
--                 for a parameter, the strongest covering reading v_scan_ledger names is full-scope; for a NULL
--                 parameter, any full catalogue reading. Dates are minute-resolution, so "at or after".
--   adjudication  an observation whose LATEST adjudication (highest adjudication_id, the rule alias and rename writers
--                 use) is not DEFERRED: a later judgment of any other outcome discharges it.
SELECT 'search' AS kind,
       'exec ' || se.exec_id || COALESCE(' ' || se.slug, '') AS subject,
       se.mined_ref_id AS ref_id,
       se.parameter_id AS parameter_id,
       se.deferred_reason AS reason,
       se.created_at AS deferred_at,
       se.created_by_session AS created_by_session
  FROM search_executions se
 WHERE se.deferred_reason IS NOT NULL
UNION ALL
SELECT 'mining',
       COALESCE(cm.global_ref_id, cm.local_ref_id) || ' ' || cm.slug,
       COALESCE(cm.global_ref_id, cm.local_ref_id),
       NULL,
       cm.deferred_reason,
       cm.created_at,
       cm.created_by_session
  FROM citation_mining cm
  LEFT JOIN evidence_sources e ON e.ref_id = COALESCE(cm.global_ref_id, cm.local_ref_id)
 WHERE cm.deferred_reason IS NOT NULL
   AND (e.ref_id IS NULL OR e.citation_mining_status = 'deferred')
UNION ALL
SELECT 'reading',
       d.ref_id || ' ' || COALESCE('parameter ' || d.parameter_id, 'whole source'),
       d.ref_id,
       d.parameter_id,
       d.reason,
       d.created_at,
       d.created_by_session
  FROM reading_deferrals d
  JOIN evidence_sources e ON e.ref_id = d.ref_id AND e.superseded_by_ref_id IS NULL
 WHERE (d.parameter_id IS NULL
        OR EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM base_parameters p
                    WHERE p.parameter_id = d.parameter_id AND p.status = 'active'))
   AND NOT EXISTS (
         SELECT 1
           FROM source_scans s
          WHERE s.ref_id = d.ref_id AND s.text_scope = 'full' AND s.created_at >= d.created_at
            AND CASE WHEN d.parameter_id IS NULL
                     THEN s.mode = 'catalogue'
                     ELSE s.scan_id = (SELECT l.scan_id FROM v_scan_ledger l
                                        WHERE l.ref_id = d.ref_id AND l.parameter_id = d.parameter_id
                                          AND l.text_scope = 'full') END)
UNION ALL
SELECT 'adjudication',
       'observation ' || o.observation_id || ' ' || o.ref_id || ' ' || o.surface_form,
       o.ref_id,
       NULL,
       a.rationale,
       a.created_at,
       a.created_by_session
  FROM term_adjudications a
  JOIN observed_terms o ON o.observation_id = a.observation_id
 WHERE a.outcome = 'DEFERRED'
   AND a.adjudication_id = (SELECT MAX(b.adjudication_id) FROM term_adjudications b
                             WHERE b.observation_id = a.observation_id);

def defer_reading(ref_id: str, parameter_id, reason: str, session: str, dry_run: bool = False):
    """Record that a READING of a source is owed and deliberately not done yet (migration 141, T-079, AT-17).

    "Deferred is okay so long as it runs eventually" (owner, 2026-09-18): a deferral is legitimate when it is on the
    record with its date, so it can be listed and aged (`v_deferred_acts`). A pair no one has read is NOT-READ in
    `v_scan_ledger` whether or not anyone decided to wait; this row says someone did, and why. THIS VERB WRITES
    reading_deferrals AND NOTHING ELSE: the pair stays owed in the ledger, and the deferral is discharged by DERIVATION
    when a full reading covers it (the view reads `v_scan_ledger`, never a flag a writer sets). `parameter_id` None
    defers the whole-source catalogue reading.

    REFUSES: a blank reason; an unknown or superseded source (the replacement is what is owed: `_refuse_tombstone`);
    a parameter that does not exist or is not active; a pair a full reading already covers, or, for the whole source,
    a source with no active parameter left without one (nothing is owed); a pair that already has a standing deferral
    (asked of `v_deferred_acts`, the one definition of "standing"). A partial, fragment or abstract reading covers
    nothing here, as in the ledger."""
    reason = dbcore.require_reason(reason, "defer-reading",
                                   "A deferral that cannot say why is neglect, and the reason is what its age is read against.")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        ref = dbcore.fold_ref(ref_id)
        if conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM evidence_sources WHERE ref_id = ?", (ref,)).fetchone() is None:
            raise Refusal(f"defer-reading: {ref_id!r} is not an admitted source.")
        _refuse_tombstone(conn, ref, "defer-reading")
        if parameter_id is not None:
            prow = _parameter_row(conn, parameter_id, "defer-reading")
            if prow["status"] != "active":
                raise Refusal(f"defer-reading: parameter {parameter_id} is {prow['status']}; a reading is owed only "
                              f"for an active parameter. Nothing was written.")
        # Owed = the ledger's own reading of the pair: a FULL reading is the only thing that covers it.
        owed = conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM v_scan_ledger WHERE ref_id = ? AND parameter_id IS COALESCE(?, parameter_id) "
                            "AND COALESCE(text_scope, '') <> 'full' LIMIT 1", (ref, parameter_id)).fetchone()
        if owed is None:
            raise Refusal(f"defer-reading: a full reading already covers "
                          f"{ref + ' for parameter ' + str(parameter_id) if parameter_id is not None else ref + ' for every active parameter'}"

def defer_reading(ref_id: str, parameter_id, reason: str, session: str, dry_run: bool = False):
    """Record that a READING of a source is owed and deliberately not done yet (migration 141, T-079, AT-17).

    "Deferred is okay so long as it runs eventually" (owner, 2026-09-18): a deferral is legitimate when it is on the
    record with its date, so it can be listed and aged (`v_deferred_acts`). A pair no one has read is NOT-READ in
    `v_scan_ledger` whether or not anyone decided to wait; this row says someone did, and why. THIS VERB WRITES
    reading_deferrals AND NOTHING ELSE: the pair stays owed in the ledger, and the deferral is discharged by DERIVATION
    when a full reading covers it (the view reads `v_scan_ledger`, never a flag a writer sets). `parameter_id` None
    defers the whole-source catalogue reading.

    REFUSES: a blank reason; an unknown or superseded source (the replacement is what is owed: `_refuse_tombstone`);
    a parameter that does not exist or is not active; a pair a full reading already covers, or, for the whole source,
    a source with no active parameter left without one (nothing is owed); a pair that already has a standing deferral
    (asked of `v_deferred_acts`, the one definition of "standing"). A partial, fragment or abstract reading covers
    nothing here, as in the ledger."""
    reason = dbcore.require_reason(reason, "defer-reading",
                                   "A deferral that cannot say why is neglect, and the reason is what its age is read against.")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        ref = dbcore.fold_ref(ref_id)
        if conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM evidence_sources WHERE ref_id = ?", (ref,)).fetchone() is None:
            raise Refusal(f"defer-reading: {ref_id!r} is not an admitted source.")
        _refuse_tombstone(conn, ref, "defer-reading")
        if parameter_id is not None:
            prow = _parameter_row(conn, parameter_id, "defer-reading")
            if prow["status"] != "active":
                raise Refusal(f"defer-reading: parameter {parameter_id} is {prow['status']}; a reading is owed only "
                              f"for an active parameter. Nothing was written.")
        # Owed = the ledger's own reading of the pair: a FULL reading is the only thing that covers it.
        owed = conn.execute("SELECT 1 FROM v_scan_ledger WHERE ref_id = ? AND parameter_id IS COALESCE(?, parameter_id) "
                            "AND COALESCE(text_scope, '') <> 'full' LIMIT 1", (ref, parameter_id)).fetchone()
        if owed is None:
            raise Refusal(f"defer-reading: a full reading already covers "
                          f"{ref + ' for parameter ' + str(parameter_id) if parameter_id is not None else ref + ' for every active parameter'}"
                          f", so no reading is owed. Nothing was written.")
        held = conn.execute("SELECT deferred_at, created_by_session FROM v_deferred_acts WHERE kind = 'reading' "
                            "AND ref_id = ? AND parameter_id IS ?", (ref, parameter_id)).fetchone()

               needs_code: str = None,
               parameter_id: int = None, absence_class: str = None,
               gap_id: str = None, form_ids=None, dry_run: bool = False) -> int:
    """Append one row to search_executions. Returns its exec_id.

    `form_ids` are rowids of term_aliases rows, read now (T-026): the forms this search
    fired. One search_execution_forms row per distinct form is written with that form's KEY
    (term_id, alias, language), never the rowid, which the capture path does not carry.
        return run_cli("log-search", "--results-found", "1", "--language", "EN", "--query-text", f"fixture N: {label}",
                       "--engine", "manual", "--depth-method", "scoping", "--session", S,
                       "--prior-expectation", "fixture prior, written before the call", *extra)

    n_before = counts("search_executions")
    r = ls_bare("names nothing")
    record("N01", "log-search refuses a search naming no slug, parameter or mined source, and writes nothing",
           r.returncode != 0 and "names what it looked for" in (r.stdout + r.stderr)
           and counts("search_executions") == n_before, f"rc={r.returncode} {(r.stdout + r.stderr)[-200:]}")
    r = ls_bare("unknown parameter", "--parameter", "999999")
    record("N02", "an unknown --parameter is refused naming its registry, and writes nothing",
           r.returncode != 0 and "has no matching row in" in (r.stdout + r.stderr)
           and counts("search_executions") == n_before, f"rc={r.returncode} {(r.stdout + r.stderr)[-200:]}")
    r = ls_bare("parameter only", "--parameter", str(PARAM))
    row = q("SELECT slug, parameter_id FROM search_executions WHERE query_text=?", "fixture N: parameter only")
    record("N03", "a search naming only a parameter is stored with a NULL slug",
           r.returncode == 0 and row == [(None, PARAM)], f"rc={r.returncode} {r.stderr[-200:]} {row}")

    def ls_cand(exec_id, *extra):
        return run_cli("add-candidate", "--exec-id", str(exec_id), "--disposition", "PENDING-VERIFICATION",
                       "--title", "fixture N candidate", "--surfaced-in", "transcripts/README.md",
                       "--surfaced-quote", "single home for what the agents actually did", "--session", S, *extra)

    (ex_bare,) = q("SELECT exec_id FROM search_executions WHERE query_text=?", "fixture N: parameter only")[0]
    (ex_slug,) = q("SELECT exec_id FROM search_executions WHERE query_text=?", "fixture M: live codes")[0]
    c_before = counts("search_candidates")
    r_no = ls_cand(ex_slug)

def merge_parameter(from_id: int, into_id: int, reason: str, session: str,
                    dry_run: bool = False):
    """Fold parameter `from_id` into `into_id`: two names for one quantity become one.

    Sets the folded row to status 'merged' with merged_into = the survivor -- the shape
    base_parameters' own CHECK has carried since 071 with no writer -- and RE-POINTS
    every row that holds the folded parameter_id at the survivor, with a dated MERGED
    line appended to each moved row's notes, in one transaction. The set of tables is
    READ FROM THE LIVE SCHEMA (every foreign key into base_parameters.parameter_id,
    including base_parameters.merged_into, so a chain of merges flattens onto the
    survivor); `_MERGE_KEEPS_HISTORY` is the only exception list, each entry with its
    reason. A table that holds the id but has no notes column is refused rather than
    moved silently.

    REFUSES: the same id twice; a blank reason; either parameter not active; a LIVE
    determination or an OPEN gate on either. K02 then holds the survivor's next
    determination to every extraction it gained.
    """
    if from_id == into_id:
        raise Refusal("merge-parameter: --from and --into are the same parameter.")
    reason = dbcore.require_reason(
        reason, f"merge {from_id} -> {into_id}",
        why="A merge that cannot say why two names are one quantity cannot be reviewed.")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        a = _parameter_row(conn, from_id, "merge-parameter --from")
        b = _parameter_row(conn, into_id, "merge-parameter --into")
        for r, side in ((a, "--from"), (b, "--into")):
            if r["status"] != "active":
                raise Refusal(
                    f"merge-parameter {side}: parameter {r['parameter_id']} "
                    f"({r['canonical_en']!r}) is {r['status']}, not active. Nothing was "
                    f"written.")
        _refuse_live_work(conn, from_id, "merge-parameter --from")
        _refuse_live_work(conn, into_id, "merge-parameter --into")
        stamp = dbcore.now()
        line = f"parameter_id {from_id} -> {into_id} (merge-parameter): {reason}"
        moved, kept = {}, {}
        tables = [t for (t,) in conn.execute(
            "SELECT name FROM sqlite_master WHERE type = 'table' ORDER BY name")]
        for t in tables:
            for fk in conn.execute(f'PRAGMA foreign_key_list("{t}")').fetchall():
                if fk[2] != "base_parameters" or (fk[4] or "parameter_id") != "parameter_id":
                    continue
                col = fk[3]
                n = conn.execute(f'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "{t}" WHERE "{col}" = ?',
                                 (from_id,)).fetchone()[0]
                if not n:
                    continue
                if t in _MERGE_KEEPS_HISTORY:
                    kept[f"{t}.{col}"] = n
                    continue
                cols = dbcore.columns(conn, t)
                if "notes" not in cols:
                    raise Refusal(
                        f"merge-parameter: {t}.{col} holds {n} row(s) for parameter "
                        f"{from_id} and the table has no notes column to record the move "
                        f"on. Moving them silently would leave no trace on the rows; add "
                        f"the table to _MERGE_KEEPS_HISTORY with its reason, or give it a "
                        f"notes column, in a tooling PR. Nothing was written.")
                info = conn.execute(f'PRAGMA table_info("{t}")').fetchall()
                pk = [r[1] for r in sorted((r for r in info if r[5]), key=lambda r: r[5])]
                key = pk or ["rowid"]
                rows = conn.execute(
                    f'SELECT {", ".join(chr(34) + k + chr(34) for k in key)}, notes '

def annotate_parameter(parameter_id: int, note: str, session: str, dry_run: bool = False):
    """Append a dated, attributed line to a parameter's notes. Never overwrites.

    The correction route a wrong note lacked (critique F18: parameter 12's note says "no
    source adjudication behind it" while TERM-091 carries a NAMES-NEW adjudication). Any
    status: correcting the record of a retired parameter is still a correction.
    """
    note = (note or "").strip()
    if not note:
        raise Refusal("annotate-parameter: --note is required and may not be blank.")
    if " || " in note:
        raise Refusal("annotate-parameter: --note contains ' || ', the separator every "
                      "dated line in notes begins with; it would make one annotation read "
                      "as two. Nothing was written.")
    with connect(dry_run) as conn:
        row = _parameter_row(conn, parameter_id, "annotate-parameter")
        stamp = dbcore.now()
        sets = {"notes": dbcore.append_dated_note(row["notes"], "ANNOTATED", session,
                                                  note, stamp)}
        sets.update(_updated(conn, "base_parameters", session, stamp))
        conn.execute("UPDATE base_parameters SET " + ", ".join(f"{k} = ?" for k in sets)
                     + " WHERE parameter_id = ?", list(sets.values()) + [parameter_id])
        return {"parameter_id": parameter_id, "annotated": True, "dry_run": dry_run}
